transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-03
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~64 minutes
Attendees: Lina Park (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Maya O'Neill (Redwood CSM), Samir Khan (NovaThera CTO), Elena Ruiz (NovaThera SRE), Marcus Lee (NovaThera PM)

Summary:
Quick rehearsal + alignment on rollback and containment for last week's cascading timeouts. Goal: validate runbook steps, confirm telemetry gaps, assign owners for a dry-run in staging.

Topics:
- Root cause recap (KV cache exhaustion + backpressure)
- Immediate mitigations and automated fallback order
- Rollback choreography and safepointing
- Observability gaps and runbook updates
- Timeline for staging dry-run and production schedule

Action items (recorded during call):
- Raj to deliver cache logs and a condensed timeline of token storms
- Elena to schedule and run failover test in staging cluster
- Lina to update and circulate containment playbook v2
- Marcus to finalize success metrics for rollback

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lina Park: alright everyone, thanks for joining, we know you had a rough week so we want to walk through a clean rehearsal of the rollback and the containment steps, um, make sure the playbook works and that telemetry will show the right indicators, ok?
[00:18] Samir Khan: yeah thanks. quick recap from our side — we saw a sudden spike in long-tail latencies after a model rollout, KV cache filled up and then the backpressure cascaded to the request router. Some requests timed out, and retries amplified the load.
[00:35] Elena Ruiz: uh yes and just to add we saw about a 3x increase in open connections on the serving pool, cpu and gpu usage were fine, it was memory-backed KV growth and the prefix cache retention that poisoned throughput.
[00:52] Raj Patel: (chiming) right, in our postmortem the sequence was model variant mismatch -> larger seq lengths from a small seg of traffic -> cache blowout, our fallback didn't trigger early because the route rules were falling back to the same variant, basically a routing loop, not a policy fail per se.
[01:10] Marcus Lee: sorry can I ask, when you say fallback didn't trigger, is that the automatic fallback in Redwood Dedicate — I mean Dedicated — or was that part of the customer's config?
[01:24] Raj Patel: good question. The automatic policy exists but the rollout config pinned a canary with sticky routing. So policy could have fallen back but the sticky affinity kept sending to the unhealthy pool.
[01:39] Samir Khan: oh wow, we thought sticky was safe. We didn't realize it could prevent fallback.
[01:45] Lina Park: yeah that's a common gotcha, sticky affinity and canary pins can block the runtime's automated fallback. That's why our playbook suggests a kill-switch route rule — a global override — for severe latency SLO violations.
[02:02] Elena Ruiz: can you show that in the playbook? a snippet?
[02:07] Lina Park: yep, Raj will share the snippet after the call. it's in the containment section, step 3b, called global-fallback-override.
[02:16] Raj Patel: i'll paste it, it's a small kebab of json — (laughs) i mean, a chunk of json. but also note we added a delay buffer to avoid oscillations.
[02:29] Marcus Lee: ok, so for today's run through — what's the choreography? who presses what button, how do we set safepoints?
[02:36] Maya O'Neill: i'll run the timeline: phase 1 detect, ops alert, phase 2 containment (global override + reduce batch sizes), phase 3 traffic shed to legacy model, phase 4 rollback if containment doesn't reduce the incident score.
[02:49] Samir Khan: incident score? how is that computed?
[02:52] Raj Patel: it's a weighted metric: p99 latency, error rate, and queue depth. threshold for auto-fallback is p99 > 800ms for 5 minutes and q depth > X where X is cluster-specific.
[03:07] Elena Ruiz: about telemetry gaps — our ops said the kv cache growth curve wasn't visible in the dashboard until after we started paging. we need earlier indicators.
[03:16] Raj Patel: we missed an export. there's a scrape lag for the cache metrics in our agent on older infra. we'll include a short-term alert on cache growth (delta per minute) and a medium-term fix to reduce agent scrape interval.
[03:29] Samir Khan: that would help. also can we get a synthetic traffic test that simulates long sequences so we can validate before rollout?
[03:36] Lina Park: yes, we can provide a canary harness — a small script that puts a controlled seq length distribution and tests preflight. we'll share it as a gist and a k8s job.
[03:46] Marcus Lee: sounds good. If we do the dry-run we want to verify both the containment steps and the rollback, and the time to switch models. what's realistic?
[03:55] Raj Patel: in our tests, model swap fallback took about 12-18s median when the KV cache warmed, worst-case 45s under load. But with the global-fallback-override + cache trim step, we get sub-30s usually.
[04:11] Elena Ruiz: is there a cache-trim API we can call to evict prefixes gracefully?
[04:16] Raj Patel: yes, there's a trim endpoint, but it's rate-limited per-pod. we run a staggered trim across pods to avoid creating a thundering herd. the playbook includes the stagger window.
[04:27] Samir Khan: okay, so for the rehearsal we should test trim-first then fallback if trim doesn't recover.
[04:33] Lina Park: agreed. order: trim -> global fallback override -> route to legacy -> rollback. That order reduces coup effects.
[04:41] Marcus Lee: what about partial traffic shaves? can we route, say, 30% to legacy first?
[04:45] Raj Patel: yes that's canary percent-based routing, we recommend progressive shift: 10% -> 30% -> 100% with health checks at each increment. But with KV exhaustion you sometimes need an emergency 100% cut.
[04:58] Elena Ruiz: and for rollback success criteria — what are we validating?
[05:01] Marcus Lee: from product side: p99 < 300ms and error rate < 0.5% within 10 minutes of rollback.
[05:09] Samir Khan: ops adds: connection depth back to baseline and no retry storms for 15 minutes.
[05:14] Lina Park: ok we'll put those in the checklist.
[05:18] --- (20 minutes of detailed runbook walkthrough, snippets and cross checks omitted for brevity) ---
[25:20] Raj Patel: (reads) step 6, run the KV diagnostics: collect top-20 prefixes, prefix hit ratios, and recent evictions. share logs to the incident channel. note: some hostnames in logs might be obfuscated and the agent transcribed as 'host-thingy' sometimes, so correlate by pod id.
[25:38] Elena Ruiz: i've got a question on the rollback artifact. do we need to revert model artifacts in object storage or just update the route config?
[25:45] Raj Patel: usually just route config is enough. you only need artifact revert if the new model has destructive schema changes. this was purely perf-related so route change suffices.
[25:56] Samir Khan: okay good. we don't want to re-deploy weights.
[25:59] Lina Park: note though, if the new variant kept runtime changes like kv serialization changes, that could be sticky even after routing back. check compatibility.
[26:11] Marcus Lee: noted.
[26:14] Elena Ruiz: about the telemetry lag fix — what's the shortest timeline to get earlier cache alerts?
[26:19] Raj Patel: short term: add an immediate alert on increase (delta) using the agent metric we already push — that's a config change, 24-48 hours. longer term: tune scrape intervals and increase retention on the critical metrics, that's weeks.
[26:33] Samir Khan: we want the short-term alert now. Elena, can you do that?
[26:37] Elena Ruiz: yes i'll create the alert and tie it to PagerDuty, alpha channel only.
[26:41] Raj Patel: perfect. i'll include the exact metric name in the playbook so it's not ambiguous.
[26:47] --- (brief cross-talk about a deck share) ---
[27:10] Lina Park: quick callout — there were a few recognition mistakes in the automatic transcript from the last incident, e.g., our runtime called 'KV strap' in the notes but the actual name is KV cache. sorry the auto-voice got weird.
[27:22] Samir Khan: (laughs) yep saw 'KV strap' — thought it was a new feature.
[27:26] Raj Patel: ok next: dry-run logistics. proposed window: staging on 2026-09-09, run at 02:00 UTC for lowest traffic. we need a 2 hour block including prep and cool-down.
[27:41] Marcus Lee: 02:00 UTC works. Who needs access? Elena will run the job but Samir and I should be notified.
[27:50] Elena Ruiz: i'll schedule and give runbook perms to Raj and Lina.
[27:54] Lina Park: I'll be on standby for the rollback button. Raj will monitor the trim and shaping steps. Maya will observe incident timeline and record times.
[28:04] Maya O'Neill: i'll timestamp each phase, expecting detect->trim <5m, trim->fallback <10m, fallback->stable <15m ideally. We'll capture any divergence.
[28:16] Samir Khan: permission wise, for the global-fallback-override we need an owner. who is authorized?
[28:21] Lina Park: we recommend a small list: Samir (as CTO), Elena (SRE lead), and designated Redwood engineer (Lina or Raj) with MFA and an approval channel. We'll put the escalation policy in the next doc.
[28:36] Marcus Lee: legal asked about audit logs for any manual override, we need tamper-proof records.
[28:42] Raj Patel: our audit log integrates with cloud KMS and records user id, API call, and pre/post config. we'll show a sample log entry.
[28:53] Elena Ruiz: great, we need retention of 365 days for compliance — is that doable?
[28:58] Lina Park: yes that's an enterprise option, we can enable long-term retention and a read-only export path. I'll coordinate with compliance.
[29:08] --- (10 minutes covering runbook edge cases and checklist wording) ---
[39:15] Raj Patel: one more technical detail — during the incident there were multiple inflight streams holding KV references. draining those streams caused a slow decline. to speed this up we propose a 'graceful-evict' signal that marks entries as stale and forces an eviction window. we'll provide the config and the client-side hint.
[39:31] Samir Khan: that sounds risky to data fidelity — can you describe failure modes?
[39:35] Raj Patel: the hint is safe for transient prefixes; it won't evict persistent lines until the window expires. there's a read-only fallback for any evicted ones. we'll run the dry-run with low risk prefixes.
[39:48] Elena Ruiz: ok we'll test it on staging with a single tenant first.
[39:52] Marcus Lee: who documented the feature? is it in the runtime docs?
[39:55] Raj Patel: we'll add it to the playbook and link the runtime doc.
[39:59] --- (short silence, then a spotting of an unrelated procurement question) ---
[40:20] Samir Khan: procurement asked about how this affects our SLA credits — if we do a rollback and reduce window, are credits triggered?
[40:27] Lina Park: it's case-by-case. if the SLO breach was caused by a pinned rollout that was under your control, credits might not apply. We'll loop in sales for formal review.
[40:38] Marcus Lee: ok makes sense.
[40:41] --- (final recap) ---
[40:50] Lina Park: recap: Raj shares containment playbook v2 + KV diagnostic snippet by 2026-09-05; Raj to include metric names for alerting; Elena to create short-term cache delta alert and schedule staging dry-run on 2026-09-09 02:00 UTC; NovaThera to confirm rollback success criteria by 2026-09-08; follow-up meeting to review dry-run week of 2026-09-14.
[41:18] Samir Khan: all good. quick ask — can we have a short doc that maps the playbook steps to pager duties? like who pages and who hits which button?
[41:27] Maya O'Neill: yes we'll add an 'actions and owners' annex.
[41:31] Elena Ruiz: thanks everyone, the staging window is critical. We'll run a preflight tomorrow.
[41:36] Lina Park: thanks team. we'll send the checklist and links; reach out on the incident channel if anything else pops up.
[41:44] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript quality: some proper nouns were misrecognized (e.g., 'Redwood Dedicated' as 'Redwood Dedicate', 'KV cache' as 'KV strap' in auto transcripts). There is occasional overlapping talk and filler words.

References shared during call:
